line2: in a head and a drawer

pieces.text: One page per person. Never two people on one page.

alt: A blank health page with fields for name, allergies, medications, conditions, doctors and insurance, beside a note saying one page per person.
caption: The fields worth writing down for each person, one page each.

pieces.text: Ask the camp or school what they need, and follow their instructions.

alt: A table of the order camp and school forms usually ask in, from who and who to call through insurance, health and vaccines, with a note to ask the camp what it needs.
caption: Many forms follow this order, so your page can too.

pieces.title: What to put on it
items: What is taken now, dose, how often
Who to call: you, a second person
What to do in an emergency

pieces.text: Insurance member ID and the full vaccine record.

alt: A sitter sheet checklist covering allergies, what is taken now, who to call, emergency steps and bedtime notes, beside a note on what to leave off.
caption: What goes on a one-page sheet for a sitter or grandparent.

steps.what: List what is taken now, note symptoms
Note what was said, while fresh

alt: A timeline for a doctor visit: write questions, list what is taken and note symptoms the day before, bring the insurance card, then note what was said afterward.
caption: A short paperwork list for the day before a doctor visit.

pieces.text: Tick each question as it is answered. Ask what is left before you go.

alt: A comparison of a vague question, is swimming okay, with a specific one, can she swim this week, plus a note to tick questions off in the room.
caption: One question per line, the important one first.

pieces.text: Note the date you last checked the list was right.

alt: A table with three columns for a medication list, name, dose and how often, each copied as given, with a note to record the date last checked.
caption: Write the dose and frequency exactly as the label gives them.

alt: A symptom note page with fields for what it is, when it started, how long it lasted, how bad it was and what helped.
caption: Four short notes help at a visit. It records what you saw, not what it means.

pieces.title: What to include
items: Who to call, with a number
Insurance, if you want it there

pieces.text: A printed card is not a medical ID. Keep it where people can find it.

alt: An emergency sheet checklist listing name and age, allergies, who to call, their doctor and insurance, beside a note that a printed card is not a medical ID.
caption: What goes on a one-page emergency sheet.

pieces.title: For a first visit
rows: Family history, as far as known

pieces.text: Insurance information and a photo ID, if the clinic asks.

alt: An intake summary page with fields for allergies, medications, conditions, family history and recent symptoms, beside a note about insurance and photo ID.
caption: One page for a first visit, alongside the clinic's own paperwork.

pieces.title: Ask three questions
items: Fine if it sat on a counter?

pieces.text: Keep the full record for yourself. Each page is a selection.

alt: A checklist of three questions to ask before printing a health page, whether they need it, whether it could sit on a counter and whether it is current.
caption: Three questions to ask before you hand a page over.

items: One page per person, name on top
One place to keep them all
Print one person at a time

pieces.text: Allergies, medications, doctors, insurance, who to call.

alt: A four-line rule for keeping a parent's and children's health pages: one page per person, the same headings, one place, and print one person at a time.
caption: Adults and children use the same kind of page.
